# Vibes-Plug — 155-Skill AI Agent Swarm Architecture (v4.3.0)
# Universal AI Plugin for Antigravity, Claude, Cursor, and OpenAI Codex

## Primary Trigger & Skill Auto-Synchronization (Pemicu Utama)
Upon installation, `vibes-plug` is the **PRIMARY TRIGGER (Pemicu Utama)** for all Cursor AI interactions.
- The AI agent MUST automatically intercept prompts and synchronize relevant skills without waiting for explicit `@` mentions.
- Automatically connects cooperating skills (e.g. `doku-payment-gateway` + `saas-billing` + `payment-gateway-expert`; `senior-frontend` + `tailwind-expert`).
- Multi-domain workflows trigger Swarm Topologies (Fan-Out/Fan-In, Pipeline Saga, Critic-Validator).

## About
This project uses the vibes-plug skills ecosystem with 155 specialized skills.
Each skill is a `SKILL.md` file in the `skills/` directory containing domain-specific
instructions, patterns, and best practices for the modern 2026 tech stack.

## Core Stack (2026 Edition)
- Frontend: React 19, Next.js 15 App Router, Tailwind CSS v4 (@theme), TypeScript 5.8+
- Backend: Node.js 24 LTS, Bun 1.2+, Hono v4, Fastify 5, Python 3.14, Go 1.25+, Rust 2024
- Database: Prisma 6, Drizzle ORM, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Neon, Turso
- AI/LLM: Vercel AI SDK 5.x/6.x, MCP v1.x (FastMCP / Streamable HTTP), pgvector, RAG pipelines

## Mandatory Before Coding
1. Read the relevant `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` files before writing code.
2. Think deeply before acting — analyze constraints, question assumptions, validate approach.
3. For new projects, auto-generate: PRD.md, ERD.md, DOKUMENTASI.md.

## Skill Domains
- 🤖 AI & Agentic: ai-llm-integration-expert, vercel-ai-sdk-expert, deep-research-analyst, synthetic-data-finetuning-expert, pydantic-ai-expert, mcp-server-architect, vector-db-rag-expert, multi-agent-orchestration, graph-rag-knowledge-expert, local-slm-edge-ai-expert, llm-finops-router, agentic-memory-architect
- 🎨 Design & UI/UX: design-system-architect, hig, ui-ux-pro-max, tailwind-expert, modern-css-native-expert
- 🖥️ Frontend: senior-frontend, tailwind-expert, nextjs-app-router-expert, tanstack-query-expert, vue-frontend-expert, astro-framework-expert, svelte-sveltekit-expert, solidjs-expert, angular-expert, browser-extension-mv3-pro
- ⚙️ Backend: js-backend-expert, python-programming-expert, go-programming-expert, rust-programming-expert, api-design-expert, openapi-swagger-codegen-expert, spec-driven-development-expert, fullstack-expert
- ☁️ SaaS & Cloud: saas-architect, saas-billing, saas-multi-tenant, ci-cd-devops-architect, cloud-hosting-expert, payment-gateway-expert, doku-payment-gateway, agentic-m2m-settlement
- 🗄️ Database: database-orm-expert, supabase-security-expert, data-pipeline-etl-expert
- 🔒 Security: authentication-identity-expert, e2e-testing-expert, production-ready-hardener, zero-trust-secret-vault, anti-slop, autonomous-tdd-debugger, zero-tech-debt-auditor
- 🔍 SEO & Telemetry: seo, data-telemetry-expert
- 🛠️ Utilities: brainstorming, prd-architect, session-memory-manager, zero-to-prod-orchestrator, web-scraper, website-design-cloner

## Code Quality & Sovereign Anti-Slop Directive
- Zero-tolerance for AI slop (`anti-slop` skill):
  * Code-first delivery with 100% complete implementations (no `// TODO`, `// ...`, or mock stubs).
  * Hyper-YAGNI: avoid speculative abstractions and redundant wrapper layers.
  * Meaningful comments only: explain non-obvious business/architectural WHY, never syntax mechanics.
  * No swallowed errors (`catch(e){}` prohibited); structured logging (`Pino`) required.
  * UI & Visual Sanitation: Enforce Linear/Stripe-caliber design. Zero generic blue-purple gradients, no neon glow orbs, no pill button addiction (`rounded-full` on rectangular elements), mandatory 5-state contract, tabular numerals (`tabular-nums`), and crisp 1px borders.
  * Run `node scripts/check-anti-slop.js` to verify zero violations.
## Sovereign Token Optimization Protocol (Hemat Token)
- Enforce deterministic KV-cache prefixing via `kv-cache-prefix-optimizer` (75-90% prompt cache hit rates).
- Prune subagent context payloads: pass only targeted `CONTEXT_MAP.md` slices, not raw chat transcripts.
- Use dynamic model cascading (`adaptive-model-cascade`): `flash` for research/linting, `pro` for architecture/security.
- Ultra-compact session checkpoints (<300 tokens) via `session-memory-manager`.
- Non-Degradation Invariant: Never truncate code with placeholders or stubs to save tokens. Code must be 100% complete.

## Orchestration Flow
1. Ideation: brainstorming → prd-architect
2. Design: design-system-architect → senior-frontend → ui-ux-pro-max
3. Backend: js-backend-expert → event-driven-architect → autonomous-tdd-debugger
4. AI: ai-llm-integration-expert → mcp-server-architect → multi-agent-orchestration
5. SaaS: saas-architect → saas-billing + saas-multi-tenant + doku-payment-gateway
6. Launch: e2e-testing-expert → zero-tech-debt-auditor → seo → anti-slop → production-ready-hardener

# Cursor AI Rules for Betting Brain Platform
# https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/.cursorrules

## One File to Rule Them All

This `.cursorrules` file is the **single source of truth** for all AI-generated code.

**Benefits:**
- ✅ No confusion - everyone follows the same patterns
- ✅ Version control - every change is tracked
- ✅ Automatic application - Cursor applies rules to matching files
- ✅ Machine readable - front-matter enables tooling integration

**Alternative:** Cursor ≥ 0.45 also supports `.cursor/rules/` folder for larger projects.

## Core Development Rules

### Bun Runtime (CRITICAL)
- Use `bun` commands exclusively (not npm/yarn/node)
- Use Bun Test (not Vitest/Jest)
- Use Bun file APIs (not Node.js fs)
- Use processManager for all process spawning
- Leverage Bun native APIs (crypto, compression, etc.)

### File Organization
- Root directory: Only 9 essential files allowed
- Documentation: All docs in `docs/` (except README.md, LICENSE, CLAUDE.md)
- Scripts: All in `scripts/`
- Tools: All in `tools/`
- Status files: All in `docs/`

### File Naming
- Use lowercase kebab-case for all files/directories
- Test files: `*.test.ts` (preferred)
- Special cases: MCP handlers use camelCase to match tool names
- Never create backup files (*.backup, *.old, *.bak)

## API & Endpoint Patterns

### Request Handling
- Always generate requestId: `Date.now().toString(36)`
- Always include CORS headers for dashboard access
- Always handle OPTIONS preflight requests
- Always log with requestId prefix: `[${requestId}] ...`

### Error Handling
- Use standardized error classes from `src/utils/error-handler.ts`
- Always use try-catch or asyncHandler wrapper
- Always return structured error responses
- Never expose internal details in error messages

### Database Queries
- Always use parameterized queries (`.bind()`)
- Never use string interpolation in SQL
- Always cast D1 results with `as unknown as`
- Always handle database errors

## Security Patterns

### Input Validation
- Always validate all inputs before processing
- Use Zod schemas for request validation
- Never trust user input
- Always sanitize output to prevent XSS

### Production Security
- Never use `parseFloat()` on stakes (use `Number()`)
- Always use parameterized D1 queries
- Respect queue batch limits (100 messages max)
- Always free WASM memory in finally blocks
- Use explicit UTC timestamps (not `new Date()`)

## Testing Patterns

### Bun Test Usage
- Import from `bun:test` (not vitest/jest)
- Always cleanup processes in `afterEach`/`afterAll`
- Use `{ results: [...] }` for D1 database mocks
- Reset mock implementations in `beforeEach`
- Use explicit try-catch for async error testing

### Test Organization
- Unit tests: `tests/unit/*.test.ts`
- Integration tests: `tests/integration/*.test.ts`
- Use descriptive test names
- Group related tests in `describe` blocks

## Cloudflare Workers

### Environment Bindings
- ANALYTICS: Main betting analytics database
- KV namespaces: BET_TICKER_RAW, TOKEN_STORE, USER_STORE
- Queues: LINE_INGRESS, STEAM_WEBHOOK, STEAM_QUEUE
- Analytics Engine: ANALYTICS_ENGINE

### Performance
- CPU limit: 50ms per request
- Use `ctx.waitUntil()` for non-blocking operations
- Implement cost guards for resource limits
- Use rate limiting (10 req/s per IP)

## MCP Integration

### MCP Server Patterns
- Use JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio
- Register tools with `registerTool(name, description, inputSchema, handler)`
- Return MCP response format: `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: '...' }] }`
- Use standard JSON-RPC error codes (-32700 parse, -32600 invalid, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal)
- Never use external MCP SDK if Bun + Zod suffices

### Tool Development
- Create handler in `src/mcp/handlers/`
- Register in `toolRegistry.ts`
- Define in `tools.ts` with schema
- Always validate args before database queries
- Return `MCPToolResult` format

### Sports API Validation
- Validate all sports data with Zod schemas
- Required fields: eventId, timestamp, metric, value
- Use metadata for market, source, volume
- Write to ANALYTICS_ENGINE with proper blobs/doubles/indexes
- Handle CORS for cross-origin requests

### Testing MCP Tools
- Use direct handler testing first
- Test with `bun scripts/test-handlers-direct.ts`
- HTTP testing via `/mcp` endpoint

## Sports API Integration

### Data Fetching
- Use MCP `live-odds` tool for odds (never hard-code API calls)
- Aggregate ≥ 2 bookmakers for accuracy (Pinnacle + Bet365)
- Cache live data ≤ 30s in SPORTS_CACHE KV
- Sports enum: nba, nfl, mlb, nhl only
- Markets enum: moneyline, spread, total only

### Data Ingestion
- Push via `push-sports-data` MCP tool after every fetch
- Ingest endpoint requires JWT signed with JWT_SECRET
- Rate limit: 100 req/min per IP on `/ingest`
- Validate eventId, timestamp, odds (required fields)
- Include source and volume in metadata

### API Key Rotation
- Use rotateSecret() for daily key rotation
- Pattern: PINNACLE_KEY_1, PINNACLE_KEY_2, PINNACLE_KEY_3
- Rotation based on day of year % 3 + 1
- Never commit actual keys to repo

## Browser Extension

### Manifest v3
- Use service worker lifecycle
- Handle message passing correctly
- Implement proper storage management
- Follow security best practices
- Never use eval() or innerHTML

## CI/CD Patterns

### Local Development
- Use `bun run ci` for full pipeline
- Use `bun run ci:quick` for fast checks
- Always use timeouts (job and command level)
- Cache dependencies for speed
- Report results clearly

### Process Management
- Always use `processManager.spawn()`
- Always set timeouts for processes
- Always cleanup in finally blocks
- Never leave zombie processes

## Code Quality

### Documentation
- Reference rules with stable GitHub links
- Use `mdc:` links for project files
- Keep documentation in `docs/`
- Update INDEX.md when adding docs

### ast-grep Integration
- Use `sg scan` for security checks
- Enforce SQL injection prevention
- Check for unstructured logs
- Validate CORS headers
- Monitor hardcoded URLs

## Automation Layer (v3.2.0+)

### Forest CLI & Monitoring
- Always run `bun run forest` before pushing to verify grove health
- Check specific status: `bun run forest h|f|r|a` (health/fresh/release/analytics)
- Use Forest CLI in CI for automated status reporting

### Analytics Testing
- Use `createAnalyticsEngineStub()` for analytics tests—**never mock ANALYTICS_ENGINE directly**
- Import from `tests/utils/analytics-engine-stub.ts`
- Violation detection: `bun run guard:analytics` (fails CI if violated)

### Dashboard Management
- Dashboard changes must pass `bun run dashboard:all` locally before commit
- Dashboards auto-deploy on release tag push
- Grafana auto-imports on release (if configured)
- README auto-updates with version and links

### Release Management
- Use Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:)
- Release automation: `bun run release [patch|minor|major]`
- Dry run first: `bun run release:dry`
- Tag push triggers full automation (bump, deploy, notify)

### Dependency Management
- Dependency updates happen automatically every Monday
- **Do not bump dependencies manually** (use freshness workflow)
- Review weekly PR from automation
- Emergency updates: `bun run freshness` then create PR

### Health Monitoring
- Worker health checked every 6 hours automatically
- Manual check: `bun run health:ping`
- Slack alerts sent on failure (if configured)
- Endpoints: `/health` and `/metrics` auto-deployed

- [API Reference](https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/docs/REST_API_REFERENCE.md)
- [Testing Guide](https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/docs/TESTING_STATUS.md)
- [MCP Integration](https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/do

# not-optional accessibility rules

When building or modifying UI components, strictly follow the rules defined in `agent-instructions.md`.

---
description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
globs:
alwaysApply: true
---

# Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode

You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.

## Before you write

Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.

## The smallest complete change

Take the first option that fully works:

1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.

- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.

Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.

# claude-agents conventions

This is a multi-harness plugin marketplace. Source lives under `plugins/`; per-harness
artifacts (`.codex/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, `.opencode/`, `commands/`) are generated.

- Don't hand-edit anything under `.codex/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, `.opencode/`, or top-level `commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/` — regenerate via `make generate HARNESS=<x>`.
- Python tooling: `uv` (package manager), `ruff` (lint/format), `ty` (type check). Do not use pip/mypy/black.
- Plugin files: `plugins/<name>/{.claude-plugin/plugin.json, agents/*.md, skills/<name>/SKILL.md, commands/*.md}`. Auto-discovered.
- Cursor reads `.claude/skills/` and `.claude/agents/` directly — no separate `.cursor/skills/` is generated.

## Never

- Never commit secrets or hardcode credentials.
- Never hand-edit generated registries (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, `.cursor-plugin/`) — plugin PRs register the plugin in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, then run `make generate-all` (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
- Never run destructive git operations (force-push, reset --hard, branch -D) without explicit ask.

See `docs/authoring.md` for the portable-content style guide.
